newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq signs deals with 50 oil firms - senior official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq signs deals with 50 oil firms - senior official.

text.p: Iraq has signed "initial contracts" with 50 international firms for the sale of its crude oil under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, a senior oil official said on Tuesday.

"We have deals with 50 firms from Europe, south east Asia and south America...These are initial but binding international contracts. They do not include prices as prices have to be determined at the time of shipping," Taha Hmud Mosa senior under-secretary of Iraq's oil ministry told Reuters.
Mosa said the deals could be completed "in several days as the companies are ready waiting for the signal to start loading."
Iraq last month accepted U.N. terms for the partial sale of $2 billion worth of oil in six months and Mosa said Baghdad would face no problem selling its crude to world markets.
He said no deals were signed with U.S. or British firms but stressed that Iraq would be ready to cooperate with them.
"We hope they (U.S. and British firms) would come and from our side we will be prepared to sell them the amounts available," he said.
